title: Outage scenarios and routing constraints intake with Helixera
meeting_header: 2027-08-05 16:00 UTC | 48 mins | Redwood: Alex Chen, Priya Nair — Helixera: Maya Singh, Liam O'Connell, Rosa Alvarez
summary: Discovery focused on outage scenarios, multi-region routing, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, and SLOs. Key constraints: strict P95 < 150ms for chat API in EU, data residency in EU, SOC2 compliance, preference for VPC/private for PHI workloads. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with synthetic failover test. Action: send pilot scope + security pack; schedule deep-dive on network topology.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot scope doc and security package by 2027-08-09
Schedule network topology deep-dive with Helixera infra by 2027-08-11
Helixera to share traffic sample CSV and SLA targets by 2027-08-10
action_items: Alex Chen - Draft pilot scope and cost estimate - 2027-08-09
Priya Nair - Prepare network deep-dive slides and sample failover scripts - 2027-08-11
Maya Singh - Share traffic distribution and P95/P99 targets, redaction of PHI flows - 2027-08-10
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya from our infra team is with me. Quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here, CTO at Helixera. We handle patient genomics pipelines, some PHI, so compliance is a hard requirement.
[00:14] Liam O'Connell: Liam, SRE lead. I run platform and we're the ones who care about failover and latency numbers.
[00:19] Rosa Alvarez: Rosa, product; I'm mostly here for availability impact on UX.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya, engineering at Redwood — focus on runtime, routing, fallbacks.
[00:29] Alex Chen: Great. Goal for today: understand outage scenarios you worry about, constraints on routing (EU-only data, V P C boundaries), and what success looks like for an evaluation — then propose a pilot.
[00:38] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Our topline: we have a chat assistant used by clinicians — P95 needs to be under 150 ms for EU traffic. We can't send any PII or raw genomics data out of EU. Also we want audit logs, SOC2 and export controls, obviously.
[00:52] Priya Nair: Understood. A few clarifying q's — is the 150ms P95 end-to-end for prompt->response or just inference time?
[01:00] Liam O'Connell: End-to-end as perceived by our web client. We have front-end to edge, so ideally our buffer is tiny. Inference token rate needs to be low latency too.
[01:09] Alex Chen: We can break that down — network + inference + streaming. For Hosted we have EU regions, but for PHI we'd recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with isolation. Is private deployment a hard requirement or preference?
[01:21] Maya Singh: If we can meet SOC2 and keep data residency, dedicated might work. Private is preferred for fully air-gapped audits but might be tougher on timeline.
[01:31] Rosa Alvarez: Also cost. Private license is heavy. If Dedicated can guarantee isolation and audit logs, that's attractive.
[01:38] Priya Nair: On reliability: Redwood supports routing policies by region, by latency and by capacity. Typical pattern is hot-primary in EU-West and hot-standby EU-Central or failover to a compatible quantized model.
[01:48] Liam O'Connell: What's the fallback behavior if EU-West loses a zone? Do requests route to another region outside EU or do they fail?
[01:55] Priya Nair: Policy configurable. We can fail closed (reject) or failover to EU-Central. We also have options to return degraded fast-fail responses or queue with a circuit breaker. For PHI we can enforce strict residency and fail closed to avoid leaving EU.
[02:10] Maya Singh: Good. What's the expected additional latency when we failover to EU-Central?
[02:14] Priya Nair: Typical inter-region adds 30–80 ms depending on path and network. With our runtime optimizations, inference delta is small; network mostly. If you prefer no cross-EU hops, we can keep cold-standby in the same region but that increases cost.
[02:28] Alex Chen: Tradeoff: cross-region failover keeps lower committed cost but adds latency/risk. Hot-standby in-region is more expensive but meets strict SLOs.
[02:37] Liam O'Connell: Do you do canary routing and automatic rollback if latency spikes?
[02:41] Priya Nair: Yes — we have traffic steering with canaries and automatic fallback thresholds. You define P95/P99 budgets and we cut traffic or revert to previous model or region.
[02:50] Rosa Alvarez: How do you surface these decisions in console? We need clear runbook integration.
[02:54] Alex Chen: Console shows per-route latency breakdown, token cost, and has a manual/auto rollback toggle. We also provide tracing hooks for SRE.
[03:02] Maya Singh: Ok, baseline question — if we did Dedicated, could we run a synthetic failover test where you simulate an EU-West outage and we measure client-facing P95?
[03:10] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We can coordinate a 2-week pilot with a scheduled failover window and shared test harness. We usually run synthetic traffic sims and collect P50/P95/P99 across regions.
[03:19] Liam O'Connell: For the pilot, we'll need to inject our own traffic patterns. We'll share a sample CSV. Can the pilot include KV cache warmup tests? Our workloads have long prefixes.
[03:28] Priya Nair: Yes, we support KV cache priming and prefix caching. We'll instrument cache hit rates as part of the pilot metrics.
[03:34] Alex Chen: Quick note on security — we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and provide audit logs for all inference requests. For Private, logs can be customer-controlled; for Hosted we retain logs per retention policy but can export to your SIEM.
[03:46] Maya Singh: Is there any chance logs contain raw PHI in hosted mode? We want guaranteed separation.
[03:51] Priya Nair: Hosted can be configured to never persist request payloads — redaction + no-storage mode — but we usually recommend Dedicated/Private for PHI workloads to avoid any ambiguity.
[03:59] Rosa Alvarez: Are there SLA credits tied to latency? Most providers tie credits to uptime, not latency.
[04:03] Alex Chen: Redwood's Dedicated contracts include latency targets (P95) and we attach SLO breach clauses; SLA credits can be negotiated for enterprise tiers. Hosted has published uptime SLAs but limited latency guarantees.
[04:14] Liam O'Connell: For routing: can we set rules like 1) if EU-West ingress latency > 80ms route to EU-Central, 2) if EU-Central degraded then circuit-breaker fail closed?
[04:24] Priya Nair: Yes — our policy engine supports multi-condition rules: latency thresholds, error rates, capacity. Circuit-breaker can be configured to fail closed for residency constraints.
[04:32] Maya Singh: What about cost impact? Hot-standby in-region seems expensive. Any heuristics?
[04:37] Alex Chen: Typical customer patterns: mission-critical endpoints get hot-primary + hot-standby (higher commit). Less critical routes use hot-primary + cross-region cold standby with fast failover for short bursts. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization profiles to save tokens.
[04:50] Rosa Alvarez: Can Optimize tune quantization without degrading clinical QA? We need to run evals.
[04:55] Priya Nair: Yes — Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload and we run evals against your prompt sets to estimate regressions. We can tie regression alerts to the pilot.
[05:03] Liam O'Connell: Network: our infra sits behind a corporate proxy and strict egress rules. How does Private handle this?
[05:09] Priya Nair: Private gives you full network control — customer-managed routing, peering, and on-prem bundles if needed. Dedicated can live in your VPC via a managed VPC peering model. We'll show network diagrams in the deep-dive.
[05:18] Maya Singh: We need a runbook for partial degradation — e.g., model returns "I can't help right now" vs returning stale cached answer. Which do you prefer?
[05:25] Alex Chen: That is configurable. Typical pattern: prioritized fallback order: native model -> quantized variant -> cached answer -> graceful degrade message. For clinical safety, many customers choose cached or degrade message rather than risky hallucination.
[05:38] Rosa Alvarez: Does Redwood provide observability for degraded answers so product can surface a label like "possibly stale"?
[05:42] Priya Nair: Yes — metadata tags can be added to responses to indicate fallback path, model variant, and cache source so the UI can show a banner.
[05:50] Liam O'Connell: About testing — will Redwood run chaos tests or do we need to run them?
[05:55] Priya Nair: We can run coordinated chaos tests during the pilot — e.g., simulate node failures, network blackholes, and region drain. We'll provide scripts and logs for postmortem.
[06:04] Maya Singh: Great. From a timeline perspective, how quickly can we start a Dedicated pilot?
[06:08] Alex Chen: Typically 2–3 weeks to provision Dedicated reserve capacity in EU if we have a signed pilot MOU. Private takes longer. If you have strict procurement timelines, we can front-load the security docs during the provisioning.
[06:18] Maya Singh: We'll need the SOC2 + pen test report and an architecture diagram.
[06:22] Alex Chen: We'll bundle our security pack and SOC2 summary in the packet to send.
[06:26] Rosa Alvarez: On measurements: we'll want to collect token-level cost, per-route P95, and cache hit ratio.
[06:31] Priya Nair: Those are standard telemetry items; we'll share a sample dashboard.
[06:35] Liam O'Connell: If during pilot we see P95 exceed 150ms, do you have automated knobs to route a percentage of traffic to a faster model?
[06:42] Priya Nair: Yes — on thresholds you can trigger traffic split to a lower-latency model variant or reduce response length. All controlled by per-route policies.
[06:49] Maya Singh: Any gotchas around KV cache when you switch regions? Warm cache stays local, right?
[06:54] Priya Nair: Correct, KV is region-local; cross-region failover will cold-start cache, so we instrument cache warming strategies and recommend sticky sessions or pre-warmed keys for critical paths.
[07:06] Alex Chen: We should capture the failure modes you care about. Could you list top three?
[07:10] Maya Singh: 1) full region outage (EU-West), 2) network partition between app and inference mesh, 3) accidental data egress policy violation.
[07:18] Liam O'Connell: I'll add a 4th: traffic storm from a runaway job.
[07:21] Priya Nair: For 1) we provide routing/failover policies. For 2) we have circuit breakers and graceful degradation. For 3) we enforce residency rules and can fail closed. For 4) rate limits and token throttles at route level.
[07:34] Rosa Alvarez: Let's talk acceptance criteria for the pilot — what's needed to call it successful?
[07:38] Maya Singh: For us: 1) P95 <= 150ms in normal and failover windows for 95% of tests, 2) no PHI left outside EU during tests, 3) visibility in the console and logs, 4) runbook and postmortem from Redwood.
[07:50] Alex Chen: That seems doable as pilot success criteria. We'll formalize in the scope doc.
[07:54] Priya Nair: I'll include failover test plan: synthetic load, chaos events, cache warmup, and a checklist for security verification.
[08:03] Maya Singh: Cost estimate is important — we need a rough committed cost vs bursty option comparison.
[08:08] Alex Chen: We'll include committed Dedicated pricing tiers and optional hot-standby uplift. Also modeled token costs with Optimize suggestions.
[08:15] Liam O'Connell: On the contract — can we get a short-term pilot MOU rather than full enterprise terms to speed start?
[08:20] Alex Chen: Yes, we have a pilot MOU template for 30-day/60-day pilots. For Dedicated we typically do 2-week provisioning + 14-day pilot.
[08:28] Rosa Alvarez: Any requirement for Helixera infra engineers to be on calls during failover tests?
[08:32] Priya Nair: We recommend one SRE on-call for coordination; Redwood provides runbook and a test channel.
[08:39] Maya Singh: Ok. Let's talk briefly about edge cases — if the model variant used for fallback has degraded quality, how will you alert us?
[08:46] Priya Nair: We tie quality regressions to prompt sets: if degraded outputs exceed a threshold we fire alerts, block the model rollout, and notify SRE/product. We'll include those thresholds in the pilot config.
[08:57] Alex Chen: Quick note: competitors like Anthropic push simpler hosted only options; Redwood focuses on unified routing and private options.
[09:05] Rosa Alvarez: That helps. Anything else we should cover before we close?
[09:09] Liam O'Connell: Can you share a sample network diagram showing where private connectors and peering will sit?
[09:14] Priya Nair: Yes — that's part of the deep-dive. We'll also include packet flow for VPC peering and private links.
[09:20] Maya Singh: Perfect. Recap and next steps please.
[09:24] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood to send pilot scope + security pack (SOC2 summary, pen test) by 2027-08-09. Helixera to share traffic samples and P95/P99 targets by 2027-08-10. Schedule network deep-dive for 2027-08-11. Pilot provisioning estimate 2–3 weeks for Dedicated, pilot window ~2 weeks with scheduled failover tests.
[09:43] Rosa Alvarez: Sounds good to me.
[09:45] Maya Singh: Agreed. We'll review the packet and circulate internal stakeholders.
[09:48] Alex Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite.
[09:52] (call ends)
